lesson.menu_desc: Reading a status update, and saying what is done, what is not done yet and what happened -- 34 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 4 -- Where We Are Now
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Juliana dos Santos Morais | Lesson 4 -- Where We Are Now
lesson.grammar_point: present perfect (already, yet, just, so far) vs past simple for status updates

listenings.text: OK, here is my update for the business breakfast. First, what we have done. We have sent all the invitations, and so far fifteen companies have confirmed. We have also booked the room at the hotel. We signed the contract last Thursday. Second, what is pending. The final menu is still pending, because the hotel has not sent the prices yet. I called them this morning, and they promised an answer by Friday. And third, the big question: are we on track? Yes, we are. The event is on track for the twelfth of November.

I need to be honest with you. We have fallen behind on this project. Here is what happened. In August, our main contact at the partner company left her job, and for a month nobody answered our emails. That was the setback. Since then, we have made some progress. We have met the new contact twice, and we have sent her all the documents again. She has read the draft of the agreement, but she has not signed off on it yet. So today we are about three weeks behind the plan. It is not a disaster, but I wanted you to know.

paras: In a partnership meeting, somebody always asks the same question: where are we now? Many people answer with a long story. They start at the beginning and explain every step. After two minutes, the others have stopped listening. A good status update is different. It has three lines, and it answers three questions.

The first line says what the team has done since the last meeting. We have sent the invitations, we have signed the agreement. The second line says what is still pending, and why. The budget is pending, because the director has not signed off on it yet. The third line says if the project is on track or if it has fallen behind. If there was a setback, one sentence is enough: the venue cancelled last week, so we have looked for a new one.

Partners from other countries often prefer this format, because it is easy to follow in a second language. It also helps the person who takes the minutes. And there is one more advantage. When your update is short, people have time to ask questions, and the meeting becomes a real conversation about the next steps.
